label: Roles
description: What the unit is for: its job or the targets it is best against, never how it does it (mechanics are patterns). A card has one primary role and up to two secondary roles. Requires says what a unit needs before it can claim a role. A source unit never claims a role whose requires it fails. If such a role still fits, leave it out and record it in fit_notes (path roles, wanted: that role). Meeting the requires is not enough: the role description must fit too. Official text means words the game or its makers wrote: the in-game role line, tooltip or production text, the manual, the official unit profile and patch notes. It still counts when read through a page that copies it. A wiki's own words (its infobox labels, prose and tables), strategy guides and internal file names are not official text; the registry notes say which infobox fields copy in-game text. For a unit recorded once for several sides, official text counts only when every side's version carries it. Official words name a role only through the role's label or one of its aliases. These words name no role: main battle tank; light, medium or heavy tank; core or line infantry; multipurpose; general-purpose; attack (as in attack helicopter); and support when it means firepower (combat support, fire support, artillery support, close air support). How to pick the primary and secondary roles is under roles in docs/fields.md. The tie-breaks settle close calls.

terms.label: Frontline assault
terms.description: Leads pushes, soaks damage and brawls at short to medium range.
terms.source_rule: As primary: any generalist that is not fast with light or no armour (step 5 of roles.primary).

terms.label: Anti-air
terms.description: Brings down aircraft, including jets and airships in high air.

terms.label: Artillery / siege
terms.description: Hits from very far, from above or over cover; breaks defences and structures.
terms.source_rule: A lobbed weapon that reaches long or further, bombs dropped from the air, a deploy mode whose gun reaches long or further and hits an area, or a long-range weapon the source says is built to break structures. A long-range missile or cannon alone is not siege, and a team that sets up its gun before firing is not deploying.

terms.label: Marksman / overwatch
terms.description: Holds long sightlines and picks off targets with precise shots.
terms.source_rule: Only a sniper weapon (the sniper family) that reaches long or further. A long-range missile gives the anti role for its target; a long-range splash or lobbed gun is siege.

terms.label: Scout / recon
terms.description: Finds, spots and marks enemies; usually fast and fragile.

terms.label: Transport
terms.source_rule: Needs two or more passenger seats. A carrier with one seat is not a transport, whatever the source calls it; its seat shows in crew.passengers and its carry-passengers or passenger-sets-weapon pattern.

terms.label: Infiltrator / saboteur
terms.description: Gets inside enemy units or buildings, or passes as one of them, to spy, steal or sabotage: steals vehicles or money, spies on or shuts down buildings.

terms.label: Disabler / control
terms.description: Stops enemies from acting: stun, root, silence, freeze, slow.

terms.label: Raider / flanker
terms.description: Hits and runs, picking off isolated targets: fast flankers, gunships that make attack runs.
terms.source_rule: As primary: a fast or very fast generalist with light or no armour (step 5 of roles.primary). As secondary: see roles.secondary.

terms.label: Area denial
terms.description: Controls ground with mines, fire, turrets or fortifications.

terms.label: Buffer / aura
terms.description: Makes nearby allies stronger for a time (more damage, armour, speed or accuracy) with an aura or a timed call. Spotting is scout; healing and resupply are support; spawn points and buildings are engineer.

terms.label: Engineer / builder
terms.description: Builds, converts or takes over structures that serve the team: barracks, outposts, spawn or supply points, bridges.

terms.label: Logistics
terms.description: Earns, carries or delivers resources for the team: harvesting, salvage, supply runs.

tie_breaks.rule: Damage first is a raider, information first is a scout. Speed alone makes a scout only when official text calls the unit a scout (by the label or an alias, such as recon). Otherwise scout needs an information part with an in-game basis: long sight, a sensor trait, stealth, or a mark or reveal ability.
Finding and marking enemies is scout; buffer is for making allies stronger.
A disabler acts on units; area denial acts on ground.

A gun line that holds ground only by the threat of its fire (a sieged tank) is siege or an anti role. Area denial needs something that stays on the ground: mines, a lingering zone, turrets or fortifications.

Mines, wire, walls, tank traps and turrets that block or guard ground are area denial. Engineer is for buildings that serve the team (barracks, outposts, spawn or supply points, bridges) and for taking buildings over. Repairing or healing is support.

Capturing map control points is a game-mode rule, so a faster capture rate supports no role. Engineer needs structures the unit builds, neutral buildings it converts, or enemy buildings it takes over and keeps. Logistics needs resources the unit gathers, carries or earns by its own action. Infiltrator needs spying, theft or sabotage from inside.

Ask what the unit does once it gets in or onto its target. If it destroys a unit (an infesting drone, a charge stuck to a tank), use the anti role for that unit: anti-armour for vehicles, anti-infantry for soldiers. If it takes over a building and keeps it, it is an engineer. Infiltrator is for spying, theft and sabotage from inside, or for passing as the enemy. A fast unit that hunts workers or harvesters from outside is a raider.
